stem.text: Let \( f(x) = 3 \ln\left(1 + \frac{x + 4}{6}\right) \). The Taylor series for f about \( x = -4 \) is \( \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{3 (-1)^{n+1} \left(x + 4\right)^{n}}{n \cdot 6^{n}} \). Does the series converge to f at \( x = -10 \)? Give a reason for the answer.

answer_key.label: No, because \( x = -10 \) is an endpoint that the interval of convergence \( -10 < x \le 2 \) excludes.

worked_solution.text: The ratio test gives convergence for \( \left|x + 4\right| < 6 \), the interior \( -10 < x < 2 \), and \( x = -10 \) is an endpoint.
At \( x = -10 \) the series is \( \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{-3}{n} \), a multiple of the harmonic series, which diverges, so the interval of convergence is \( -10 < x \le 2 \).
